name: Shop Page Manager for eCommerce
author: zamartz

sections.description:
Shop Page Manager for eCommerce changes what the WooCommerce shop page and the product category pages list, without editing products. You set up a rule set: what to hide, and the condition under which it is hidden.

What a rule set can hide:

  • Products in chosen categories, chosen products, products with chosen variations, products with chosen attribute values, and products whose price is less than, greater than or equal to a price.
  • Categories in the category list: chosen categories, categories that hold a chosen sub-category, categories that hold chosen products or variations, and categories whose number of products is less than, greater than or equal to a number (empty categories count as 0).

When it applies: when the number of published products (“Active Product Count on page”) is less than, greater than, equal to or not equal to a number you choose. The count is of the whole catalog with the shop page’s product filters applied; on a product category page it still counts the whole catalog, not only that category.

One master switch turns the rule set on or off. It is on the settings screen and in the Customizer, under WooCommerce > Product Catalog.

Everything above is free and complete. Nothing in this plugin is locked or needs a license.

The settings are under ZAMARTZ > Settings > Plugins > Shop Page Manager for eCommerce, and the same settings are under WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Shop Page Manager. Administrators and WooCommerce Shop Managers can change them.

Paid add-on

A separate paid add-on, sold on zamartz.com, adds more. It is a second plugin that you install beside this one; its settings appear in the same places as the free ones. Shop Page Manager for eCommerce: Paid Add-On adds:

  • More rule sets, each with its own condition, a priority to set the order they are checked in, and “Stop other rules”.
  • More conditions: available product count on the page, order subtotal, customer roles, products, variations or categories in the cart, an applied coupon, and the total quantity in the cart.
  • The Visual Customizer: edit the rule sets in the Customizer and preview the shop page as you change them.
  • The shop page, the add to cart behavior and the catalog defaults (shop page display, category display, default sorting, products per row) on the same screen.
  • A network admin screen on multisite.

Works with

  • “Show products by attributes or variations” by Addify: its catalog ordering keeps working when the default sorting changes.

What this plugin sends elsewhere

  • zamartz.com: only if a site administrator says yes to “Share anonymous events” in the ZAMARTZ admin (asked once, changeable under ZAMARTZ > Settings > General). The events are activate, deactivate (with the reason chosen, if any), delete, and a click on “Review Now”. Each sends the plugin’s name, the event, and a one-way hash of the site address; never the address itself, an email, a user or order details. Saying no sends nothing. See the Zamartz privacy policy.
  • The ZAMARTZ dashboard shows news from zamartz.com only after the same yes, or when you click “Load them now”.
  • Nothing is sent from the shop pages your visitors see.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install this plugin from Plugins > Add New, and activate it.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Shop Page Manager (or ZAMARTZ > Settings > Plugins).
  4. Switch on “Shop Page Manager”, choose what to hide and when, and save.
sections.faq:
My rule set does not hide anything

Check that the “Shop Page Manager” switch is on, and that the condition is met on the page: for “Active Product Count on page”, the number is the count of published products in the catalog (with the shop page’s filters, but not the category of a category page), before anything is hidden. A page cache may still show the page as it was; clear it after saving.

Where is my paid license?

From version 4.0.0 the paid features are in a separate paid add-on. Your license, your settings and all of your rule sets are kept on your site. Download the add-on from your account on zamartz.com, install it beside this plugin, and the paid features come back with no need to enter the license again. Until then, only the first rule set applies, and only when its condition is “Active Product Count on page”, as on the free version before.
sections.changelog:
4.0.0

This is a major update.

  • Changed: the paid features moved to a separate paid add-on, available from zamartz.com. This plugin no longer holds license code or contacts zamartz.com for licenses. Sites with a paid license keep their license, settings and every rule set, and see a one-time notice with the link to the add-on.
  • Changed: “Stop other rules” (paid add-on) now stops the later rule sets only when its own rule set’s condition is met. Before, a rule set with “Stop other rules” on stopped every later rule set even when its own condition was not met.
  • Changed: one settings section, shown both under ZAMARTZ > Settings > Plugins and under WooCommerce > Settings > Products > Shop Page Manager, with one save. The WooCommerce entry stays at its old address and now shows even while the switch is off. WooCommerce Shop Managers can now save it.
  • Changed: the ZAMARTZ admin updated to 2.4.2 (security fixes, per-section permissions, assets loaded only where needed, translated with this plugin’s own text domain; a failed save now says so instead of staying on “Saving…”, every dropdown has a name screen readers announce, and the settings description names the other screen the settings are on).
  • Changed: the text domain is now shop-page-manager-for-woocommerce, the plugin’s WordPress.org slug, so WordPress.org language packs apply.
  • Removed: the promise of scheduled rule sets in this readme. Scheduling was never part of the plugin.
  • Fixed: the price rule cut prices to whole numbers ($19.99 was compared as 19), changed every other query on the page, and hid products with no price. It now compares the exact price, on the shop’s product query only, and never hides a product that has no price.
  • Fixed: “Not Equal To” was offered but never matched.
  • Fixed: a category product count rule never matched empty categories (“less than 1” or “equal to 0”).
  • Fixed: “Has Attributes” hid only the first ten products with the attribute.
  • Fixed: a settings save could write any option whose name contained the plugin’s prefix (license options included), and any option at all through a special field name; it now saves only this plugin’s listed settings, and only for users who may manage WooCommerce.
  • Fixed: the form’s searches and requests had no permission or nonce check.
  • Fixed: on a site in another language, a translated “Free” label could switch features on or off.
  • Fixed: deleting the plugin deleted nothing (the option names were misspelled). It now deletes its own settings and rule sets, and never the license or the paid add-on’s settings (the add-on removes those when it is deleted).
  • Changed: a rule set saved with a paid add-on condition can now be switched to the free condition. Until you do, “Keep the saved condition” leaves it as it is.
  • Fixed: an empty script and stylesheet were loaded on every page of the site, and the admin script and style on every admin screen.
  • Fixed: Addify’s catalog ordering handler was not replaced when Addify loaded after this plugin.
  • Compatible with WordPress 7.1, WooCommerce 11.3, PHP 7.4 to 8.5, WooCommerce order storage in custom tables and the cart and checkout blocks.

3.2.0

  • Updates to accepted product ids. (Released with version number 3.1.0 in the plugin header.)

3.1.0

  • Major version update.
  • Improved compatibility with WordPress 6.8.1.
  • Enhanced compatibility with WooCommerce 9.9.5.
  • Performance optimizations.
  • Bug fixes and stability improvements.

1.3.0

  • Level set (no substantial updates).

1.2.0

  • Default sorting issue fix.
  • Paid version alert issue fix.

1.1.0

  • ZAMARTZ core update.
  • Updated to work with DIVI categories.

1.0.1

  • Design and readme fix.

1.0.0

  • First release.
